title: Bubble timing, held bubbles, shortcut words and the handle's state
owns: app/main/agent/presenter.ts, app/renderer/overlay/target-copy.ts and the bubble/overlay renderer, app/main/agent/host.ts (bubble parts), app/main/targets/runtime.ts (offers), app/main/commands/window.ts + copy.ts (announcement words), app/main/handle.ts state; shared hunks in main.ts

items.title: "More time to read and answer" is applied twice to any bubble that waited or was covered, so it stays 100 times its usual time instead of 10
items.scenario: More time is on (readTime 10). Case 1: a task finishes while the user is reading the conversation's answer. Its result (claim "reply") waits, then shows when the answer goes, and stays 885 s instead of 88.5 s. For that time it holds the bubble, so other tasks' progress can't show, and overlay.ts keeps Ember parked (a finished done/idle/error message counts as waiting), so Ember stops following the pointer for about 15 minutes. Case 2: an unasked ssh or WSL offer (OFFER_MS 25 s) that waited behind an answer stays 2500 s, not 250 s, with Ember held still beside its buttons. Case 3: "Hey Ember" that was another word gives an answer back (claimBubble, then releaseBubble), and the answer stays 688 s, not 68 s. Every further cover multiplies by 10 again. Any answer that finished behind a question is affected too.
items.evidence: hideLater() scales the time and stores the scaled value: presenter.ts:666-668 (ms = base*scale), then pendingHide = ms at :670 or hideMs = ms at :671. letGo() copies the scaled hideMs into pendingHide (:615-618). reshow() calls hideLater(this.pendingHide) at :635, which multiplies by the scale again. I ran a scratch vitest file on an export of HEAD (scratchpad/xreview/bubble/tree/test/unit/xreview-readtime.test.ts) with a real BubbleOwner and Presenters, readTime = readTimeOf(true). Results: "offer stayed 2500.01 s on screen (expected 250 s)", "answer stayed 688.01 s after it was given back (expected at most 68 s)", "task result stayed 885 s (expected 88.5 s)". All three fail. The package's own #51 tests only cover bubbles that are on screen at once (presenter.test.ts:902-936).
items.cause: fix/bubble #51 (50ebd22, 8d95111): readTime scaling added inside hideLater, which reshow() and letGo() reuse with already-scaled times. It surfaces in every interaction that makes a bubble wait: the Confirmer's questions, main's claimBubble for Listening… and the kill switch, and the runtime's unasked offers (#14).
items.fix: Scale only once. Split hideLater(base) into hideLater(base) { this.armHide(base * scale) } and armHide(ms), which sets pendingHide or hideTimer/hideMs with no further scaling. reshow() calls this.armHide(this.pendingHide). Add the three cases above to presenter.test.ts.
items.skeptic:
I confirmed the finding on HEAD 4e47b13. The scratch tree's app/main/agent/presenter.ts is identical to the worktree's.

How it happens:
- hideLater(base) multiplies by readTime, which is clamped to 1..10 and is 10 when More time is on (presenter.ts:666-668). It then stores the scaled value, either as pendingHide when the bubble is unseen (:670) or as hideMs (:671).
- letGo() copies the scaled hideMs or pendingHide back into pendingHide (:615-618).
- reshow() calls hideLater(this.pendingHide) (:635), which multiplies by 10 a second time.

Real paths that reach it:
- A bubble that waited behind another: post() at :744, outcome/idle at :880 and :1017, then reshow when the bubble frees up.
- An answer covered by main's claimBubble: host.ts:721-722 runs owner.claim (which calls covered.letGo(), presenter.ts:205) and presenter.letGo(). releaseBubble then calls p.reshow() (host.ts:750) or covered.reshow() (:753).
- A guide step's reshow("step") (:264).
- Unasked offers do post with { ms: OFFER_MS = 25_000, claim: "reply" } (targets/runtime.ts:478, 1137, 1227).

I ran the scratch test xreview/bubble/tree/test/unit/xreview-readtime.test.ts with vitest. All 3 tests fail:
- The task result stayed 885000 ms; the expected limit was 89500 ms.
- The offer and the answer handed back were both still up at their 10x deadline.

Nothing guards against it:
- There is no cap on ms after scaling; the clamp applies only to the factor.
- The bubble report for #51 says the intent is 10x: "Unsolicited offers then last up to 250 s". So 100x is not an accepted limitation.
- Neither lead-notes nor docs mention it.

While the bubble stays up, the reshown bubble holds it as "reply", so allows() refuses other tasks' "progress". overlay.ts:138-163 counts a finished done/idle/error bubble, or one with actions, as waiting, so Ember stays parked.

Limits on severity:
- It happens only when More time is on (the default factor is 1).
- A new user request ("take") or a dismiss still clears the bubble.

Still, every bubble that waited or was covered stays 10 times longer than intended, and longer still with each further cover. So it is a real defect, though moderate rather than catastrophic. The proposed fix is correct: scale once in hideLater, and have reshow re-arm with the already-scaled time.

items.title: At the Larger text size, answers that fit six lines at 14 px lose their last line(s) with no "Read all" and no keyboard route (#12 undone by text size)
items.scenario: The user picks Settings › Comfort & access › Text size: Larger (1.3). Ember answers "Your Wi-Fi is connected to HomeNet-5G with a strong signal, but the VPN called Work-WireGuard dropped two minutes ago. Would you like me to reconnect the VPN now, or leave it off until you are back at work tomorrow?" (215 chars, answerLines = 6, so cutShort is false). The bubble keeps its 300 px width while the type grows to 18.2/26 px. The answer needs 7 lines and .eb-thought's 6lh cap shows 6. The closing question is hidden under the fade, with no Read all button and no "Or press … go to Conversation." step. A six-item list ("Here are the windows you have open:" plus 5 window lines, 194 chars) loses its last item the same way.
items.evidence: I built an export of HEAD (scratchpad/xreview/bubble/tree, npm run build) and rendered the real overlay page in Playwright Chromium (scripts/textsize-readall.mjs) with html[data-text-size]. VPN answer: default 14px/20px needs 6 lines, shows 6; larger 18.2px/26px needs 7, shows 6, 26 px hidden, data-overflow=true, 0 buttons. List answer: same result. Screenshot: scratchpad/xreview/bubble/shot-larger-215.png. presenter.ts:24 LINE_CHARS = 36 ("300 px wide, 14 px Ember Sans") and :37-39 cutShort take no text scale. packages/bubble/src/bubble.ts sets .eb-thought max-height: 6lh, and its html[data-text-size] rules scale the font but keep the width. page-prefs.ts:23 leaves the overlay out of FIXED_TYPE, so it scales.
items.cause: fix/css #57 (text size; round 2's 2e52d11 made the caps 6lh, "whole lines at every size") merged after fix/bubble #12 (e5a5f09: Read all by answerLines at 36 chars a line). Neither side, nor the css merge 9884b6a, connects the two.
items.fix: Let the presenter know the text scale. AgentHost takes textScale: () => textScale(settings.get().textSize) from main, passes it to the conversation presenter, and cutShort/answerLines use Math.floor(LINE_CHARS / scale) characters a line. Alternatively, the overlay renderer reports a finished idle thought with data-overflow and main adds ui:more. Add a pin with a 215-char answer at scale 1.3.
items.skeptic:
I could not refute it. The defect is real, though it covers a narrower range than "major" suggests.

What I checked:
- app/main/agent/presenter.ts:24 sets LINE_CHARS = 36 for 14 px type, and cutShort (:37-39) has no text-scale input. The only place that adds the "ui:more" (Read all) action is presenter.ts:979-982. main.ts:1256 only handles the button press. Nothing else adds Read all or the keyboard-route step.
- The bubble does detect the overflow: bubble.ts:622 and :687 set data-overflow. But nothing in main or the overlay reads it, so the overflow never turns into a Read all button.
- BUBBLE_CSS:379 scales font-size and line-height under html[data-text-size]. The width stays min(300px, ...), with no width rule in overlay/styles.css. The .eb-thought cap is 6lh (:282).
- page-prefs.ts:23 FIXED_TYPE excludes only ask, desk and mic, so the overlay page scales.

I ran the real code:
- I bundled HEAD's presenter.ts with esbuild (scratchpad/xreview/skeptic-ts/pres.mjs) and fed it userPrompt plus assistant.message. The 215-char VPN answer and the 194-char six-line list both come out with actions [] and step null.
- I re-ran the finder's Playwright render of the built overlay. The "Ember Sans" font was confirmed loaded via document.fonts, and the bubble's text area is 300 px wide. At the default size both answers need 6 lines and show 6. At Larger (18.2/26 px) both need 7 and show 6: 26 px hidden, data-overflow=true, no buttons.
- I swept prose answers that cutShort lets through (140+ chars). Default: 0 overflow. Large: 0. Larger: the 200-216-char ones overflow. List answers whose lines are about 29-36 chars also gain a wrapped line at Larger.

Nothing covers it:
- It is not in docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-26.
- DESIGN.md:76-82 says only the Ask box, the desk bar and the terminal type keep their size.
- The lead-notes open items and follow-ups list the terminal font and card button min-heights for text size, not this.
- css report #57 says its 6lh caps show "as many lines at every size", but never ties that to the presenter's 36-characters-a-line count.

It is not a regression against 63b88cd, which had no text-size setting. It is #12's symptom (a hidden last line, often the question, with no Read all and no keyboard route) coming back for users of the new opt-in Larger setting.

Why it is somewhat less severe than claimed:
- It only happens at Larger (Large was clean in my sweep), and only for answers of roughly 200-216 chars or lists with longish lines.
- The bottom fade shows that something is cut off.
- The full answer is still in Settings > Conversation.

I would rate it moderate rather than major, but the scenario is confirmed.

items.title: An unasked ssh offer replaces the held "Lost build-01" or "Can't connect to build-01" bubble at once, then expires and leaves nothing
items.scenario: build-01 drops ("Lost build-01 [Reconnect] [Stop trying]", held, no timer), or a connect fails ("Can't connect to build-01 [Try again] [Close]", meant to stay until closed). The user opens a terminal and runs ssh to see what happened: ssh web-07, or ssh build-01 itself, whose state is lost or closed so connected() is false. The noticer, which looks only once a computer is added (remote #33), offers "You're connected to …". Its claim "reply" should make it wait, but it shows immediately in place of the Lost or failure bubble. 25 s later it expires as Not now and the bubble empties. build-01 is still lost, and its Reconnect, Try again and the reason never come back. COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md:428 says the offer "waits until you've finished reading what the bubble shows", :475 says Lost "stays until you answer it or the connection comes back", and :613 says the failure "stays until you close it".
items.evidence: Scratch test appended to a copy of targets-runtime.test.ts (scratchpad/xreview/bubble/tree/test/unit/xreview-offer-lost.test.ts), using the file's own screenRig and rig with notice argv ["ssh","deploy@web-07"]. Output: "after the noticer: You're connected to web-07 [Bring Ember, Not now, Don't offer again]", then "after the offer expired: (hidden) ; build-01 still: lost". The failed-connect variant gives "Can't connect to build-01 [Try again, Close]", then "You're connected to web-07", then "(hidden)". Both fail. Code: every runtime bubble goes to the one NoticeBoard presenter (runtime.ts:664-670, nb.post), and Presenter.post replaces that presenter's previous bubble. BubbleOwner.allows returns true for claim "reply" when holder === p (presenter.ts:229), so the offer never waits behind the board's own held bubble.
items.cause: fix/bubble #9/#14 (all runtime bubbles share one board presenter; unasked offers use claim "reply" to wait) against its own #11/#183 (held Lost and failure bubbles). Made reachable by remote #33: offers come only once a computer is added, which is exactly when Lost and failure bubbles exist.
items.fix: Post unasked offers (showSeenOffer, offerWsl) through a second board presenter on the same BubbleOwner, for example AgentHost.offers. Claim "reply" then waits behind the held Lost or failure bubble, and the held bubble comes back after the offer goes. Or skip the offer while shown is a held key (lost:, fail:, stalled:, connecting:, or connected: with commands off) and take its key out of noticer.offered so it is offered later.
items.skeptic:
I confirmed the finding by running it. The scratch test at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/bubble/tree/test/unit/xreview-offer-lost.test.ts uses the file's own screenRig, with a real Presenter and BubbleOwner. The tree it runs in has runtime.ts, presenter.ts, offer.ts and targets-runtime.test.ts byte-identical to relfix-int HEAD; only a JSDoc comment in host.ts differs. Both cases fail:
- Lost case: "Lost build-01 [Reconnect/Stop trying]", then "You're connected to web-07 [Bring Ember/Not now/Don't offer again]", then "(hidden)" after 26 s, with build-01 still lost.
- Failed-connect case: "Can't connect to build-01 [Try again/Close]", then the offer, then "(hidden)".

The code path:
- Every runtime bubble goes through bubble(), which calls nb.post on one board (runtime.ts:664-670). main.ts:1747 wires that board as agent.notices, the single AgentHost.noticeBoard presenter (host.ts:621).
- The Lost bubble (runtime.ts:795) and the failure bubble (runtime.ts:841) post with claim "take" and no ms, so that presenter is the holder and its bubble is held.
- showSeenOffer (runtime.ts:1137) and offerWsl (runtime.ts:1227) post claim "reply" with ms OFFER_MS on the same presenter. BubbleOwner.allows returns true when h === p (presenter.ts:229), so Presenter.post replaces the held bubble at once.
- hideLater(25 s) then calls hide(), which empties the presenter's state. The replaced Lost or failure bubble no longer exists anywhere, so nothing brings it back.

Nothing guards against this:
- The noticer checks only dismissed, connected and questionUp (offer.ts:105-109). connected() counts only ready, stalled and connecting (runtime.ts:1216), so a lost or closed build-01, or any other host, is offered.
- enabled() requires hosts.length > 0 (remote #33), which is exactly when Lost and failure bubbles can exist.

Not covered elsewhere:
- docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 has no such limitation.
- Lead-notes' only related item is "#14 parking for unsolicited offers (bounded by 25 s)". That is about the pointer follower parking, not about bubble replacement.

The behaviour contradicts the packages' own claims:
- bubble #11: Lost "comes back after anything that covers it".
- bubble #14: unasked offers "wait behind an answer being read".
- Docs :428, :475 and :613.

Mitigation, which keeps it minor rather than refuting it:
- At 63b88cd an offer also replaced the Lost bubble through the single setter. There it stayed until answered instead of expiring, so this is an incomplete fix more than a new regression.
- Settings › Computers keeps build-01's state, its reason and Reconnect.

The minor severity stands.

items.title: "More time to read and answer" doesn't reach the new notices other packages added: screen-lock notices, "I can't take screenshots", "Commands are off"
items.scenario: More time is on, a setting labelled "messages stay ten times as long". (a) The user comes back to a locked screen and asks: "LOCKED_ASK" shows for 6 s (main.ts:898). The "what stopped while you were away" notice shows for 8 s (main.ts:1917). (b) macOS refuses Screen Recording mid-task: "I can't take screenshots [Open setup check]" goes after 15 s (main.ts:1547-1549). (c) The "Commands are off" hint with Open settings goes after about 10.6 s (host.ts:703). Each lasts its usual time, not ten times.
items.evidence: showNotice → holdNotice(…, ms) arms setTimeout(ms) unscaled (main.ts:889-892, screen-lock.ts:276-279). The screenshots notice uses setTimeout(…, 15000) (main.ts:1547). hintCommands builds new Presenter(…, { shortcuts }) with no readTime (host.ts:703), unlike the conversation, board and task presenters (host.ts:620-622, 1414-1415). Origins: bf22035 (screen lock, voice #81), bf0de1f (screenshots notice), e74c14d (cmdcore #40). Bubble's #51 wiring covered only hideIfStill, the Confirmer and AgentHost's existing presenters.
items.cause: fix/voice #81, the macOS screenshots notice commit and fix/cmdcore #40 each added a bubble after, or independently of, fix/bubble #51's readTime plumbing. No merge scaled them.
items.fix: In main: showNotice(n, ms) passes ms * readTime() to holdNotice, and the screenshots timer uses 15000 * readTime(). In host.ts:703: pass ...(this.o.readTime ? { readTime: this.o.readTime } : {}) as the task presenter does.
items.skeptic:
I could not refute it. All three bubbles ignore More time on the merged branch.

(a) The screen-lock notices. main.ts:889-892 showNotice passes ms straight to holdNotice, and screen-lock.ts:276-279 arms setTimeout(ms) with no scaling. LOCKED_ASK is shown with 6000 (main.ts:898) and the lock notice with 8000 (main.ts:1917). hideIfStill (main.ts:534-537) is the only main-side timer multiplied by readTime().

(b) The macOS screenshots notice. main.ts:1547-1549 uses a literal setTimeout(..., 15000).

(c) The "Commands are off" hint. host.ts:703 builds new Presenter(..., { shortcuts }) with no readTime. Presenter's constructor then defaults to () => 1 (presenter.ts:534), so outcome() hides after 6000 + 106*50 = 11.3 s (presenter.ts:880) whatever the setting. The conversation and board presenters do get readTime (host.ts:619-622), and so does the task presenter (host.ts:1415).

I ran it in a scratch vitest built on host-targets.test.ts's own harness, with readTime passed to AgentHost (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/bubble-moretime/test/unit/mt.test.ts). On the ask path (host.ts:1581) the hint goes up for a moment before "Thinking…" covers it, and its timer starts then.
- readTime 1: it shows again at 6 s and hides at 11.3 s.
- readTime 10: the answer stays 60 s, the hint's unscaled timer runs out behind it, and the hint never comes back.

So with More time on, the user can lose that hint entirely, which is worse than the finding says.

None of the ways out applies:
- No guard elsewhere scales these timers.
- lead-notes "Open interaction notes" and "Follow-ups after merge" don't mention it.
- COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 doesn't accept it as a limitation.
- The docs promise the opposite: DESIGN.md:57 says "every bubble stays ten times as long", and README.md:213 and home/index.html:182 say "messages stay ten times as long".
- The bubble report's #51 entry says only hideIfStill, the Confirmer and AgentHost's presenters were wired.

Two small corrections that don't change the verdict. The origins are fix/perception (bf0de1f) and fix/agent (e74c14d), not cmdcore; both were merged before fix/bubble (1d44566) and neither was scaled at that merge. The hint's base time is 11.3 s, not 10.6 s.

Severity stays minor: it is an accessibility setting promised in the docs, and two of these bubbles carry the only button to the fix.

items.title: The 'Commands are off' bubble (review #40) is never seen when a request triggers it, and it ignores 'More time to read and answer'
items.scenario: ask() calls hintCommands() at host.ts:1581 before the request is sent. Nothing holds the bubble at that moment, so its outcome() goes on screen at once and its hide timer starts (about 11 s). conductor.ask then puts up 'Thinking…' with claim 'take', and that timer keeps running under 'Thinking…' and the answer. commandsHinted is already set, so the answer's own trigger at host.ts:1120 ('turn commands on in settings (Commands)') does nothing. Scenario: commands are off by the user's switch, and the user types 'run df -h in the terminal'. Copilot thinks for 3 s and answers in about 170 characters. The answer stays about 14.6 s, while the hint's 11 s runs out underneath it. The hint, with its Open settings button, never shows, and it never comes back for the rest of the run. The hint's Presenter (host.ts:703) also gets no readTime, unlike the three presenters fix/bubble threaded it into (lines 620, 622, 1415). With More time on, the answer stays 10 times as long, so even the existing unit test's case (an answer-less turn) never shows the hint.
items.evidence: I wrote scratch tests built on the host-targets.test.ts fakes. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/agent/test/unit/xreview-hint.test.ts emits user.message (the fake send does), then a 170-character answer after 3 s, then session.idle. It printed 'the Commands are off bubble seen after the answer: false' at readTime 1 and 10. The same test on the fix/agent tree alone (scratchpad/xreview/agent-fx) gives the same result, so it is #40's own gap. xreview-readtime.test.ts reruns the existing host-targets case 'after the answer, a bubble says commands are off…' with readTime: () => 10. 'Commands are off' never becomes visible: the bubble trace is Thinking… until T+60000, then empty. Without readTime it is visible from 6 s to 11.3 s. git show fix/bubble:app/main/agent/host.ts shows bubble added readTime to its three presenters. hintCommands' presenter came from fix/agent (e74c14d), and merge 1d44566 left it without readTime.
items.cause: fix/agent e74c14d/e82d30a (review #40): the hint is posted at ask time and its timer runs while covered. Merge 1d44566 (fix/bubble, review #51 readTime) did not thread readTime into the presenter fix/agent added.
items.fix: Pass readTime in hintCommands' Presenter options, as on host.ts:622. Defer the hint from the request path until the conversation's turn has ended and its answer has gone: note the request at ask(), then call outcome() from the turn's end or onAnswer, or post it with a pending hide that starts only when it first reaches the screen. Set commandsHinted only once it has actually been shown. Extend the host-targets test with a turn that shows a real answer.
items.skeptic:
I confirmed this by running it, but only for typed requests. Spoken requests are fine.

Code path:
- ask() calls hintCommands() synchronously at app/main/agent/host.ts:1581, before conductor.ask.
- Nothing claims the bubble on the typed path. The IPC.ask handler (main.ts:1222) goes through askEmber to agent.ask, and openAsk never calls claimBubble. When the bubble is idle, owner.holder is null, so the hint's outcome() ('reply' claim) goes on screen at once and starts its hideLater. The text is 106 characters, so 6000 + 106*50 = 11.3 s, and no readTime is applied (host.ts:703).
- Conductor.ask (conductor.ts:529) calls presenter.userPrompt synchronously. That is a 'take' claim, which sets holder and current to the conversation presenter without calling letGo() on the hint, so the hint's timer keeps running underneath.
- When the timer fires, hide() finds onScreen false and owner.gone() false, so the hint vanishes without ever being shown.
- commandsHinted is already true, so the answer's own trigger (host.ts:1120) does nothing for the rest of the run.

What makes the gap certain: persona.ts:51 tells the model to say that commands are off, that they can be turned on in settings (Commands), and to offer to guide instead. That answer is about 180 characters, so it stays for 6000 + 50*chars, about 15 s, which is longer than the hint's 11.3 s even when Copilot answers instantly.

Scratch test /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/skeptic-hint40/test/unit/zz-skeptic-hint.test.ts, run on a git archive of HEAD bbe8ab2 with the host-targets fakes:

| Case | Bubble trace | Hint on screen |
|---|---|---|
| Typed, persona-length answer after 2 s | T+0 'Commands are off', T+0 'Thinking…', T+2000 'Ember', T+17050 empty | 0 ms |
| Typed, shortest wording, 0–1 s | hint at T+9100–10100 | only 1.2–2.2 s |
| Existing test's case (answer with no deltas), readTime 10 | 'Thinking…' until T+60000, then empty | never |
| Voice (claimBubble first, as main does on wake and speech) | hint at T+17050 | full 11.3 s |
| Voice, readTime 10 | hint at T+152500 | 11.3 s, not 113 s |

In the voice case main holds the bubble, so the hint's 'reply' claim is refused, its hide stays pending, and it shows once the answer has gone. It also shows when a previous answer still holds the bubble.

The readTime omission is real too: unlike the presenters at host.ts:620, 622 and 1415, the hint ignores 'More time to read and answer' (review #51) even when it does show.

This is a new feature from #40, so there is no regression against 63b88cd. It is not in the lead-notes open items or follow-ups, and it is not in docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1–L26.

Severity stays minor. The answer already tells the user where to turn commands on in words; what is lost is the Open settings button, for typed requests made while the bubble is idle, which is the usual first-request case.

items.title: The announcement's bubble and command window name the stop chord even when another app holds it, while the spoken line drops it
items.scenario: Another app has already registered Ember's stop chord: Ctrl+Alt+X on Linux, Win+Alt+X on Windows, or Control+Shift+Command+X on macOS. Ember's registration fails, so shortcutsTaken holds the accelerator (main.ts:1486-1488). The user then types "delete build/" and the flow announces `rm -r build` (D4.4). The bubble says "On this computer. It starts in 4 seconds. Ctrl+Alt+X stops everything at once." The command window says "Or press Ctrl+Alt+X to stop everything." Only the spoken line knows the chord isn't Ember's: it says "Press Stop to cancel." A keyboard or screen-reader user who presses the advertised chord during the countdown reaches the other app, not Ember's kill switch, and the dangerous command runs. The Stop buttons still work, so the wrong advice only affects people who use the chord.
items.evidence: Code read: the presenter builds the announcement with a fixed label. presenter.ts:529 sets `this.stopKey = (opts.shortcuts ?? SHORTCUTS.linux).stop.label`, and presenter.ts:848 passes it to `announcement(text, this.where, seconds, this.stopKey)` (target-copy.ts:143-147). The command window does the same: window.ts:360 adds `announceKeys: announceKeyText(o.os)`, and copy.ts:199-201 returns `Or press ${SHORTCUTS[os].stop.label} to stop everything.`. Neither one asks whether Ember holds the key. The spoken path does: main.ts:1799 passes `cancelWords({ killPhrase: voice?.rejectsSpeakers ?? false, stopKey: hasKey(sc.stop.accel) ? sc.stop.say : null })`, where hasKey (main.ts:541) checks shortcutsTaken. Ember already handles a taken key for the settings route (keyboardRoute(key: string | null) in target-copy.ts) and for the card's key hint (deps.keyHint holds only the keys main holds). Ran: I bundled the integration branch's copy functions into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/cmdsafety/bundles/copy.cjs and printed each OS with the chord taken. linux: bubble 'On this computer. It starts in 4 seconds. Ctrl+Alt+X stops everything at once.', window 'Or press Ctrl+Alt+X to stop everything.', spoken 'Press Stop to cancel.' win32 and darwin give the same mismatch with Win+Alt+X and Control+Shift+Command+X.
items.cause: fix/cmdwin (#46, #269) added the stop chord to the bubble's announcement and the window's countdown from the static SHORTCUTS table. fix/bubble (#22, #24) moved the bubble text into target-copy's announcement() with cmdwin's chord (merge 1d44566). fix/voice (#251) is the only one that checks whether Ember holds the chord (cancelWords with hasKey), and only for the spoken line. The three wordings of the same announcement disagree.
items.fix: Give the announcement the chord only while Ember holds it, the way cancelWords gets it. Add an option such as `stopKey?: () => string | null` (main: `() => hasKey(sc.stop.accel) ? sc.stop.label : null`), passed through AgentHost to the task presenters, and a matching `stopKey()` hook in CommandWindowOptions next to keyHint. When it is null, announcement() and announceKeyText() leave out the chord sentence and the Stop button is the only route named, as the spoken "Press Stop to cancel." already does. Pin the taken-chord case in ui-copy.test.ts and command-window.test.ts.
items.skeptic:
I confirmed the finding by reading the code and running it. It is minor, as filed.

Code paths:
- **Bubble:** app/main/agent/presenter.ts:529 fixes `stopKey` from the static table (`(opts.shortcuts ?? SHORTCUTS.linux).stop.label`). Every AgentHost presenter is built with `shortcuts: this.sys.shortcuts` (host.ts:621, 622, 703, 1126, 1415). announce() at presenter.ts:848 passes it to announcement() (target-copy.ts:143-147), which always writes "<chord> stops everything at once."
- **Command window:** app/main/commands/window.ts:360 always adds `announceKeys: announceKeyText(o.os)` while an announcement counts down. copy.ts:200-201 returns `Or press ${SHORTCUTS[os].stop.label} to stop everything.` with no taken-key input.
- **Spoken line:** only this one checks the key. main.ts:1799 passes `hasKey(sc.stop.accel) ? sc.stop.say : null`, and hasKey (main.ts:541) reads the shortcutsTaken that registerShortcuts fills (main.ts:1480-1488).
- **No fallback:** nothing elsewhere rewrites the bubble or window text, and no local handler (before-input-event or renderer keydown) catches the stop chord. When another app holds the chord globally, pressing it never reaches Ember.

Ran: I bundled the integration branch's announcement, announceKeyText, cancelWords and SHORTCUTS into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/skeptic-stopkey/out.cjs and ran it with the stop accelerator marked taken.
- linux: the bubble says "...Ctrl+Alt+X stops everything at once.", the window says "Or press Ctrl+Alt+X to stop everything.", and the spoken line says "Press Stop to cancel."
- win32: the same split, with Win+Alt+X.
- darwin: the same split, with Control+Shift+Command+X.

Not a regression in the other direction: at 63b88cd the bubble said only "On this computer. It starts in 4 seconds." and named no chord. cmdwin #46/#269 added the chord without checking whether Ember holds it, so this mismatch is new in this change.

Not already scheduled:
- lead-notes #45(b) (remappable shortcuts, a fallback chord, launcher Ask entries) is a future feature. It does not cover the copy naming a chord Ember lacks.
- The merge note "announcement wording ... + stop chord: check what the merge chose" is about the bubble #22 vs cmdwin #46 wording. It does not cover the taken-key case.
- docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-26 lists no such limitation.

Why minor: the Stop buttons in the bubble and the command window still work. The command is one the user asked for. Only someone who uses the advertised chord during the countdown is misled, and for them the command then runs.

items.title: The bubble names Ember's settings and stop shortcuts even while another app holds them (Read all's route, the D4.4 announcement)
items.scenario: Another app holds the settings chord (or the stop chord), which ask #45 detects: shortcutsTaken, hasKey() false. An answer cut short says "Or press Ctrl+Alt+E and go to Conversation." (presenter.ts:981), and a keyboard or screen-reader user who presses it triggers the other app. An announced command (D4.4) says "… It starts in 5 seconds. Ctrl+Alt+X stops everything at once." (presenter.ts:848, target-copy.ts:145). The user presses Ctrl+Alt+X, it goes to the other app, and the command runs. Meanwhile the runtime's own routes, built from the same keyboardRoute, correctly say "Or open Ember's settings and go to Computers.", and the spoken cancel words say "Press Stop to cancel."
items.evidence: Presenter's settingsKey and stopKey come from the static shortcut table (presenter.ts:528-529; AgentHost passes shortcuts: this.sys.shortcuts). keyboardRoute's contract is "`key`; null: another app took it" (target-copy.ts:155-161), and the runtime is wired with settingsKey: () => (hasKey(sc.settings.accel) ? sc.settings.label : null) (main.ts:1749). The voice cancel words check hasKey(sc.stop.accel) (main.ts:1799). Nothing passes shortcutsTaken to the presenters.
items.cause: fix/bubble #47 (round 2, 80acaa6: Read all's route) and the bubble merge of cmdwin #46's stop chord into announcement() (1d44566) use the static table. ask #45 and voice V1 made the other paths shortcut-aware.
items.fix: Give AgentHost settingsKey() and stopKey() callbacks from main (null while taken), and have the presenter read them per bubble. keyboardRoute(null, …) then gives "Or open Ember's settings…", and announcement() drops the chord sentence, or names the handle's Stop, when stopKey is null.
items.skeptic:
I could not refute it. The finding is real, and "minor" is the right severity.

1. The presenter has no way to know a shortcut is taken. Its constructor sets settingsKey and stopKey once from the static table: `this.settingsKey = (opts.shortcuts ?? SHORTCUTS.linux).settings.label; this.stopKey = (...).stop.label` (presenter.ts:528-529). Every AgentHost presenter is built with `shortcuts: this.sys.shortcuts` (host.ts:621, 622, 703, 1415). Nothing in between knows about taken shortcuts:
   - `this.sys` is `o.system ?? LINUX_WORKER_SYSTEM` (host.ts:602).
   - main passes `wslAwareSystem(sys)`, a Proxy that only swaps `apps` (wsl/privacy.ts:77-97).
   - `shortcutsTaken` is a module variable in main.ts (main.ts:175, set at 1488 by registerShortcuts). It reaches only main's own copy: hasKey (main.ts:541), the greeting, the menus, the runtime's settingsKey callback (main.ts:1749) and cancelWords (main.ts:1799). None of these touch the presenter.

2. I ran it. I bundled presenter.ts with esbuild into scratchpad/xreview/bubble-keys/run.js and fed it a 12-line answer and then an announce(), using the win32 table. The output was:
   - "Or press Win+Alt+E and go to Conversation." with the Read all action.
   - "On this computer. It starts in 5 seconds. Win+Alt+X stops everything at once."

   The presenter has no input that could change this copy while another app holds Win+Alt+X or Win+Alt+E. On Windows (RegisterHotKey) and on X11 (XGrabKey), globalShortcut.register fails when another app holds the chord, so taken is a real state there. The 60 s retry (main.ts:1491) keeps that state for as long as the other app holds the key.

3. This is not a lost merge fix. fix/cmdwin's own presenter already used the static `this.stopKey`, and the base (63b88cd) had neither the Read all step nor the chord sentence. Both texts are new copy in this release that the shortcut-taken handling from ask #45 and voice V1 does not cover.

4. Nothing excuses it:
   - keyboardRoute's own contract is "`key`; null: another app took it" (renderer/overlay/target-copy.ts:155-161).
   - The scheduled follow-ups (#45(b) remappable shortcuts and a fallback chord) and the merge note on announcement wording are about other things.
   - Nothing in COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26 covers it. README.md:219 accepts only that shortcuts can't be changed, and points users to the settings routes. The bubble should therefore not name the taken chord.

Why it stays minor: the announcement's Stop button stays visible, the command window's countdown is the authoritative Stop, and onAnnounce speaks only the flow's words, not the chord sentence. The harm is a wrong keyboard instruction. A keyboard or screen-reader user who follows it presses a key that goes to the other app, and the command starts.

items.title: A question that brings a hidden Ember back leaves the handle as the hidden-state tab until some other state change
items.scenario: The user hid Ember (Hide Ember, which since ask #75 shrinks the handle to the 56×56 face tab). A task asks a plain bubble question (no panel window). The Confirmer shows the question, and questionChanged unhides the overlay (overlay.setHidden(false)), but the handle stays the compact tab, the hidden-state look, while Ember and its question are on screen. It only becomes the pill on the next showState, which during a question is often only the ack after the answer: guardWhileAsking drops bubble writes, and the waiting worker publishes nothing.
items.evidence: The Confirmer calls show(question) and then onChange (confirm.ts:241-243). Main's showState runs syncHandle() while the overlay is still hidden (main.ts:499-505, 508), so setCompact(true) is a no-op. questionChanged then calls overlay.setHidden(false) and presenceChanged() (main.ts:818), and neither calls syncHandle(). HandleWindow.setCompact (handle.ts:97-101) is the only path back to the pill. The Hide/Show menu and the setPresence IPC both call syncHandle() after setHidden (main.ts:681, 1203).
items.cause: fix/ask #75 (compact tab driven by syncHandle in showState) against the pre-existing unhide-for-a-question path in questionChanged, which predates the tab.
items.fix: Call syncHandle() right after overlay.setHidden(false) in questionChanged (main.ts:818), as the menu and setPresence do. The same applies in askEmber's shownForAnswer branch (main.ts:901) for consistency.
items.skeptic:
I could not refute this. I read the code and ran the flow, and the finding holds at minor severity.

The flow, as read:
- confirm.ts:242-243: `next()` calls `this.show(...)` and then `this.onChange(...)`. The Confirmer is built on the unguarded `showState` (main.ts:1570).
- That `showState` runs `syncHandle()` (main.ts:505, 508) while the overlay is still hidden, so `setCompact(true)` changes nothing (handle.ts:97-101 returns early when `on === this.compact`).
- `questionChanged` then runs `overlay.setHidden(false); presenceChanged();` (main.ts:818). Neither of those calls `syncHandle()`. `OverlayManager.setHidden` only sets a flag (overlay.ts:92). `presenceChanged` only broadcasts IPC, and the handle page has no presence listener (no hits in app/renderer/handle or app/preload/handle.ts).
- The `stepAside()` call in `questionChanged` (main.ts:805) runs before the unhide, so it does not help either.

Why nothing else fixes it during the question:
- `guardWhileAsking` (confirm.ts:274-281) drops bubble, emotion and talking writes, so a patch with only those fields never reaches `showState`.
- The worker calls `confirmer.ask` from inside a tool step (worker.ts:3403). It set its detail when the step started (worker.ts:1308), so it publishes no task cards while it waits.
- Speaking the question does not change the mic state: `voice.speak` (voice.ts:262) never calls `setState`.

So with one task and no microphone activity, the handle stays the 56×56 tab for the whole question: up to 2 minutes, or 20 with More time to read and answer. It becomes the pill again only on the ack in `finish()` (confirm.ts:257). A second running task's progress, a mic state change or a status change would fix it earlier, but only by chance.

The run: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Ember-Powered-by-Github-Copilot/9df81ff3-d6fa-5078-ac02-9c8dbaa6cb03/scratchpad/xreview/handle-q/sim.ts`, bundled with esbuild, uses the real `Confirmer` and `guardWhileAsking`. The overlay and handle are stubs with the same `setHidden`/`isHidden`/`setCompact` behaviour, and the script keeps main's order. Output:
- After Hide Ember: hidden=true, compact=true.
- Question up: hidden=false, compact=true.
- A worker bubble write during the question, and again 1 s later: compact=true.
- After the answer: compact=false.

This was not lost in a merge. fix/ask's own main.ts has the same line 696 without `syncHandle`, so the #75 fix is incomplete. Against 63b88cd it is a regression, because there was no tab then and the handle was always the pill.

Nothing excuses it:
- It is not an accepted limitation in docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md L1-L26.
- common.md says nothing about it.
- It is not among the lead-notes open items or follow-ups. The #75 follow-up there is only the handle position setting.

Severity stays minor. Ember, the question and the handle menu (which reads `overlay.isHidden()` at main.ts:652) are all correct. Only the handle keeps the hidden-state size and drops its words, and `deskViewRef.handleMoved()` is not called.

The askEmber `shownForAnswer` branch (main.ts:900) has the same gap but fixes itself quickly: the agent's next bubble goes through `setState` to `showState` and `syncHandle`, and the guard does not drop it there.

The proposed fix is right: call `syncHandle()` after `overlay.setHidden(false)` at main.ts:818, and also at main.ts:900.

items.text: The merge of bubble #22 and cmdwin #46 chose one wording for the D4.4 announcement (bubble: 'On this computer. It starts in N seconds. <chord> stops everything at once.'; command window: 'Or press <chord> to stop everything.'; spoken: cancelWords). Check the three read as the same announcement (same seconds, same stop route) in every state, including the screen-reader time (#46) and V1 (no kill phrase where speaker rejection isn't running). X0 covers the taken-chord case; fix any other mismatch.

app/main/remote/registry.ts notConnectedWhy and the 'lost' reason: the merge combined remote #197's plain wording (no tool names) with the bubble package's sentence. Check each reason Ember gives for a computer it isn't connected to reads as one plain sentence, with no tool or internal names; fix if not, with a copy pin.

The greeting's reasons: the merge kept an order for why Ember can't work yet (lockdown by the organisation's policy, sign-in, setup rows...). Check lockdown comes first (it overrides the others) and each reason appears once; fix if not, with a test.

Review #263, left by cmdwin: when a command waits for the user to type, the task's bubble says 'A command is waiting for you to type in the command window.' with no way to get there from the bubble. Add a 'Show' button (or the bubble's existing action pattern) that brings the command window up and gives it the keyboard; keyboard and screen-reader reachable like the bubble's other buttons. cmdwin's full note: Round 1: attach() raises the window on every run (moveTop, no focus). window.ts awaitsTyping() looks for SECRET_PROMPT, or a short line whose words end in ':', '?', '>' or '[y/N]'. After 2 s at such a prompt the tab shows 'Waiting for you to type in this window.', the window is raised and flashFrame'd, and onWaiting listeners are told. flow.ts followWaiting puts 'A command is waiting for you to type in the command window.' in the task's bubble. A time limit reached while waiting gets its own status line. Round 2 (verifier's should-fix): followWaiting returned early on waiting=false, so the bubble kept the waiting line. It now remembers the bubble's thought before the waiting line (presenter.bubble). When the run stops waiting (typing, or the run ending), it puts that thought back, or 'The command is running.' if the bubble was empty, but only while the bubble still shows the waiting line, so newer words stay. Docs §2.2 says the line lasts until you type or the command ends. Left: a 'Show' button on the bubble (bubble and task actions belong to the presenter and bubble packages), an OS notification, and pausing the time limit while it waits. The limit is §3.13's safety bound; changing it is a design decision, so the status line says it was waiting instead.
